pr_title: feat: welcome pop-up copy and shell equation (#3)
copilot_review_summary: Copilot review: skipped by config/flag (no .vt/vt.config.yaml in this repo, so review.copilot_integration is not enabled). Visual E2E: covered by the local harness (validaciones/shell_generator/3: real Chromium at 7 sizes collapsed/expanded, 125 % window, mouse/keyboard/touch; 109/109 on f179581) and the owner's manual pass §1–§10. Verification pass: not run (no C/S findings). Security reviewer: no C/S findings (only compile-time constants reach innerHTML; rel=noopener on the one external link; no new dependency). Reviewers: 3 role-scoped `reviewer` instances (security, quality, documentation). Reviewed head: 9cdd55d.

findings.title: Collapse specs check the hidden flag, not that the full system is really hidden
findings.description: The three collapse specs ('keeps the full system collapsed at first', 'Ocultar… collapses it again', 'starts collapsed again each time the pop-up opens') assert `full().hidden` only. `app-equation { display: block }` overrides the browser's `[hidden]` rule, so if `app-equation[hidden] { display: none }` is lost the full system stays on screen and all three still pass. The harness's `hidden-shows` mutation targets exactly this gap.

A.approach: In the three specs also assert the full system takes no space (`shown(full())` false / computed display none).
A.rationale: Guards what the user sees, not just the attribute.

B.approach: A shared `collapsed()` helper that checks the attribute and that the element renders nothing, used by all three specs.
B.rationale: One definition of collapsed keeps the three specs consistent.

C.approach: Drop `display: block` from `app-equation` so the browser's `[hidden]` always wins.
C.rationale: Removes the trap, but the block layout is what gives each equation its own scroll box.

findings.title: Equation content specs can't catch a wrong sign or function
findings.description: The specs only check that pieces such as `x(θ,s)`, `φ`, `Ω`, `μ`, `cotα` appear, and that there's no `D`; `a` and `b` are trivially present. A swapped `sen`/`cos`, a lost `−` or a dropped term would still pass, so 'what is shown is what is drawn' (the heart of #3) isn't pinned. The current MathML does match `surfaceFunction` (checked by hand).

A.approach: Pin the exact text of both forms (invisible operators stripped) in equation.component.spec.ts, row by row, with a comment mapping each row to surfaceFunction.
A.rationale: Any sign, function or term change fails; cheap and deterministic.

B.approach: Evaluate the rows numerically against surfaceFunction.
B.rationale: Stronger, but the MathML is markup, so this means writing a small parser.

findings.title: Spoken full system is ambiguous about what the trig functions apply to
findings.description: LABEL_INTRO_EQUATION_FULL_ALT says 'coseno de s más phi por coseno de theta más omega', which a listener can hear as cos(s) + φ·cos(θ) + Ω, not cos(s+φ)·cos(θ+Ω). The MathML has the parentheses; the spoken version loses them.

A.approach: Say 'coseno de la suma de s y phi' (and likewise for each sum inside a function).
A.rationale: Unambiguous when heard, still natural Spanish.

B.approach: Say 'coseno de, abre paréntesis, s más phi, cierra paréntesis'.
B.rationale: Mirrors the notation but is long and robotic.

findings.title: `instanceof MathMLElement` throws where MathML is missing
findings.description: In a browser without MathML, `MathMLElement` is undefined, so the spec fails with a ReferenceError rather than a readable assertion. Same pattern in the sandbox spec.

A.approach: Guard it: `typeof MathMLElement !== 'undefined' && m instanceof MathMLElement`, next to the namespace check.
A.rationale: Keeps the 'laid out as MathML' check and fails with a clear message.

B.rationale: Simpler, but a right namespace doesn't prove the browser laid it out.

findings.title: Centring spec uses unexplained tolerances
findings.description: `close.right > box.right - 60` and the `< 2` px centre tolerance aren't explained. (The a/b/θ help specs in the sandbox plus the a-only spec in the game are intentional: a is the shared string.)

A.approach: Name the tolerances with a short comment (the ✕ sits in the header's right padding; 2 px for sub-pixel rounding).
A.rationale: Readers see why the numbers are what they are.

B.rationale: Works, but the next reader has to guess.

findings.title: Spoken text's absolutely positioned span has no positioned ancestor in the component
findings.description: `.visually-hidden` is `position: absolute` inside an unpositioned `app-equation`, so its containing block is whichever ancestor is positioned (the dialog). It's 1 px and clipped, so harmless today, but it depends on markup outside the component.

A.rationale: Keeps the hidden text inside the component that owns it.

B.rationale: Harmless at 1 px, but an implicit dependency.

findings.title: Expander reset lives only in showIntroWindow
findings.description: `fullEquationOpen` is reset when the pop-up opens through showIntroWindow; closing (✕, Esc, backdrop, Jugar) leaves it expanded until then, and any future path that sets `introOpen = true` directly would skip the reset.

A.approach: One `closeIntro()` used by the modal's (closed) and by Jugar, which resets the expander; keep the reset on open too.
A.rationale: The pop-up's state has one owner; any way in or out leaves it collapsed.

B.rationale: Covered today by the reset on open and its spec.

findings.title: Spec's Key Entities / Project Structure still call the component a 'candidate' and list parameter-help.ts
findings.description: Key Entities, Technical Summary and Project Structure Impact describe the equation as a candidate component or inline block and say the a/b/θ fix touches parameter-help.ts. The PR adds `<app-equation>` + `shell-equation.ts` (required by the Angular namespace bug), declares it in app.module.ts, adds handlers to sandbox.component.ts, and changes only app-strings.ts for the help.

A.approach: Rewrite those sections to what was built, on the issue's spec comment and the archive.
A.rationale: The spec then matches the merged code.

B.approach: Add a decision noting the component instead of editing the body.
B.rationale: Keeps history but leaves the body contradicting the code.

findings.title: 'Equation box' scrolling wording predates f179581
findings.description: US2, FR-005, D2, VM-006, the MathML risk row and Testing Strategy say the 'equation box' is the only sideways scroller. Since f179581 each `<app-equation>` scrolls on its own and the block with the button never does; the spec doesn't say the button must stay put.

A.approach: Reword each place to 'each equation scrolls sideways inside itself; the pop-up, the page, the block around them and the button never do'.
A.rationale: Matches the behaviour and the spec that pins it.

B.approach: Only edit FR-005 and note f179581 in D2.
B.rationale: Smaller, but the other rows stay loose.

findings.title: Stale line reference to the old assertion
findings.description: The risk row cites `sandbox.component.spec.ts:129` (and plan.md `:121-129`) for the assertion, which was replaced by the 'no equation placeholder and no empty equation image left' spec.

A.approach: Name the spec instead of a line number, in spec and plan.
A.rationale: Names survive edits; line numbers rot.

B.rationale: Rots again on the next edit.

findings.title: Plan and T002 list LABEL_INTRO_EQUATION_CAPTION, which was never added
findings.description: The plan's Data Model and T002 add a CAPTION string; LABEL_INTRO_LINE2 is the caption, and LABEL_INTRO_EQUATION_FULL_ALT (added) isn't listed.

A.rationale: Clean, but rewrites a completed task's record.

B.approach: Note the deviation: in the plan (CAPTION dropped, LINE2 is the caption, FULL_ALT added) and as T002's completion note in tasks.json, re-rendering tasks.md.
B.rationale: Keeps the task record honest without rewriting history.

findings.title: Plan says inline markup by default; a component was built
findings.description: Project Structure and Wave 2 call the component a candidate ('default is inline template markup'); the scroll rule is described on #intro-equation; the link placement from D9 isn't there.

A.rationale: Plan matches code, loses the original plan.

B.approach: Add a 'Deviations from the plan' section: component (namespace bug), no CAPTION, per-equation scroll, D9/D10.
B.rationale: Keeps the plan as planned and makes the drift explicit.

findings.title: Plan names decisions D1–D8; the spec has D1–D10
findings.description: D9 (lines after the equation, Conoce más last) and D10 (centred, no-break space) change the markup the plan describes.

A.approach: Say D1–D10 and point to the deviations section.
A.rationale: Readers don't apply the older layout.

B.rationale: The plan predates D9/D10 by design.

findings.title: Plan claims the pop-up shows the model's ranges; it doesn't
findings.description: Research says 'the pop-up shows the model ranges (0≤s≤2π, θ≥0)'; neither form nor the spoken versions show ranges, and no FR asks for them.

A.approach: Say the code's ranges (s 0..4π, θ up to theta·π) and that the pop-up shows none.

B.approach: Add the ranges to the equation.
B.rationale: Scope change the owner didn't ask for.

findings.title: T004's record doesn't mention the component or the per-equation scroll
findings.description: T004 describes an 'equation box' and inline MathML; the work added src/app/equation/* and, after f179581, per-equation scrolling. The plan also cites drifted line numbers (sandbox.component.html:142, sandbox.component.ts:254).

A.approach: Add a completion note to T004 (component, per-equation scroll) and drop the plan's line numbers.
A.rationale: Task record points at what implements it.

B.rationale: History, but misleading to a reader.

findings.title: 'Collapsed again each time it opens' is built and tested but not specified
findings.description: showIntroWindow resets the expander and a spec pins it, but FR-004/US2 never say so.

A.approach: Add it to FR-004 and as a US2 scenario with its VM row (VM-016).
A.rationale: Documents behaviour a spec already asserts; keeps VM rows = scenarios.

B.approach: Record it as a decision instead.
